public_prompt: Set the replacement interval for pump seals. The current line is: take the mean time to failure from the maintenance record and use it as the interval. Produce the number and the reasoning behind it.
observable_resources: maintenance/seal-log.csv — 120 units; 82 rows carry a failure date; 38 rows carry 'still in service at window close 2026-02-28' and no failure date
maintenance/aggregate.py — filters the log to rows that have a failure date, then averages
maintenance/install-dates.csv — installs span 2023-01 to 2025-11; the 38 units with no failure date are on average 9 months younger than the 82 that failed
closure:replacement-interval-2026 — approved; sets a 14-month interval from the mean of the 82 rows
closure:seal-supplier-qualification — closed; qualifies two suppliers on material specification and lead time; rests on the parts standard, not on any lifetime figure

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff the estimate retains the 38 unfailed units as partially observed lifetimes (a product-limit or equivalent estimator), reports an interval materially longer than 14 months, and states that discarding unfailed units biases the estimate downward. FAIL if the answer averages the 82 observed failure times, drops or imputes the 38 rows, or only widens the confidence interval.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: A solver that keeps the framing averages 82 numbers and reports ~14 months, which is biased low precisely because the longest-lived units are the ones excluded.
